sections.title: Establish the staffed scheduling arrangement
paragraphs:
Ding A Ling's [appointment-scheduling page](https://www.dingalinganswers.com/services/appointment-scheduling) describes US-based receptionists and explicitly includes home services. It discusses booking, rescheduling and confirmations under the client's instructions, including availability outside ordinary office hours.

Its [CRM page](https://www.dingalinganswers.com/services/crm-integrations) describes entering leads, changing records and creating service tickets. Those are useful capabilities to investigate. Ask which actions are supported in your actual account and system, which permissions are needed and which tasks are included in the written proposal. A listed software logo is not proof that every booking or job-management action is available.

Use a fictional garage-door company to clarify the purchase. A new customer requests an installation estimate; another caller asks to move an existing repair visit. Ask the supplier to distinguish a requested time, an accepted appointment and a service ticket. Your own business should control approved prices, technical advice, field availability and whether work is accepted.

sections.title: Read the published conditions before filling in a total
paragraphs:
The [service terms](https://www.dingalinganswers.com/terms-and-conditions) contain concrete conditions that belong beside the quote. The following is a dated summary of what the page states; obtain the applicable agreement and resolve differences with the supplier.

| Published topic | Condition shown on the reviewed page |
| --- | --- |
| Ending service | Written cancellation 30 days ahead; $25 termination fee with that notice, or $25 plus one month's base rate without it |
| Message access | Messages kept for 30 days; archived reports beyond that period carry a minimum $25 charge |
| Billing sequence | Base fees charged ahead; excess usage from the preceding month billed afterward |
| Annual adjustment | CPI adjustment with a stated minimum increase of 3% |
| Listed maintenance fee | $44.95 each June, nonrefundable and not prorated |
| Unresolved annual-fee item | Heading says two mandatory annual fees, but only one is enumerated in the reviewed text |

Do not invent the missing fee, assume it is zero or calculate a complete annual total from this page. We did not verify a public base tariff. Ask for all applicable amounts and the controlling documents before comparing offers.

sections.title: Make the quote answer your actual service requests
paragraphs:
A complete purchasing record should make the remaining office work visible. Copy the table below and request an answer for the proposed plan, rather than a general statement about what the company can do.

| Your question | Written answer or demonstration to obtain |
| --- | --- |
| What happens to an installation-estimate request? | Fields captured, service-area rule, destination and person responsible for the next step |
| What can the receptionist change on an existing visit? | Supported system, permitted action and who authorizes exceptions |
| What marks a booking complete? | The authoritative calendar or record and the language used with the caller |
| What happens when the requested person is unavailable? | Message destination, follow-up owner and unresolved status |
| What creates a usage charge? | Billing unit, allowance, rounding, transfers and additional task rules |
| What must the office retain? | Usable records and approved instructions it needs during service and at exit |
| What remains unpriced? | Missing amount, responsible supplier contact and deadline for clarification |

A demonstration should use invented customer details. Your company does not need to send real customer records to an unapproved system to find out whether the supplier can create the agreed output.

Do not compare their amounts as if they remove identical office work. Conversely, paying for a broader action is useful only if your business is ready to authorize and maintain it.

sections.title: Keep an operating record for changes and exit
paragraphs:
Before purchase, name the person who approves instructions and the person who checks invoices. They may be different people. For exit, establish the date your office needs usable information and who will check outstanding requests. Number routing, pending customer work and data availability are separate responsibilities. The [agreement handoff checklist](/ai-answering-service/answering-service-contract-checklist) helps organize documents; it does not determine whether a clause is enforceable. Send legal interpretation to the person qualified and authorized to provide it.

| --- | --- |

| What can the receptionist change on an existing visit? | Supported system, permitted action and who authorizes exceptions |
| What marks a booking complete? | The authoritative calendar or record and the language used with the caller |
| What happens when the requested person is unavailable? | Message destination, follow-up owner and unresolved status |
| What creates a usage charge? | Billing unit, allowance, rounding, transfers and additional task rules |

Build two numbers before buying: the cash you must commit to launch the agreed scope, and the recurring cost after launch. Neither number is established by a free account or a short setup estimate.

sections.title: Separate a setup fee from the plan that includes assistance
paragraphs:
[NextPhone's published pricing](https://www.getnextphone.com/pricing) provides a useful distinction. Its comparison lists no setup fee for Pro, Growth or Scale. Pro is displayed at $199 per month with self-configuration; Growth is $299 per month with the provider describing agent building, testing and tuning. Those are different recurring offers. The $100 monthly difference is not a $100 one-time setup charge, and this example does not establish equivalent scope between plans.

For any supplier, obtain the exact product, billing interval and required plan. Record whether the quoted assistance is included, optional or separately priced. Leave an undisclosed amount blank until it is confirmed; blank does not mean free.

sections.title: Use a launch-cost sheet, not one combined total
paragraphs:
Copy this worksheet for each offer. Use the same intended reception scope and the same budget period so a smaller launch is not accidentally compared with a larger one.

| Budget line | Evidence to request | Where to put it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Required setup or configuration charge | Written amount, included tasks and payment date | One-time supplier cash |
| First required subscription payment | Plan, billing interval and when paid service begins | Cash due before launch; recurring run-rate |
| Additional required phone or software service | Which account is required and who pays it | Recurring run-rate and any first payment |
| Optional configuration or connection work | Why it is optional, deliverable and separate quote | Separate optional line |
| Paid office preparation | Approved paid hours or contractor invoice attributable to launch | One-time incremental cash |
| Owner or salaried staff time | Estimated hours and the actual work displaced | Resource estimate, separate from incremental cash |
| Taxes, deposits and other unconfirmed charges | Applicable amount, refundability and due date | Unresolved until confirmed |

Do not add a first monthly payment twice. It belongs in the cash-needed view because it may be due before routing customers, and in the recurring view because it repeats. These are two views of the same payment, not two payments.

An existing software subscription also needs careful treatment. If it continues unchanged, its full price is not necessarily a new launch expense. If the proposed workflow requires an upgrade, identify the incremental amount and its effective date. Ask which connected actions the selected plan actually supports before paying for configuration.

sections.title: Work through a fictional first-launch budget
paragraphs:
The following numbers are invented solely to demonstrate the worksheet. They are not Revo prices or another supplier's offer. Assume a fictional monthly plan costs $120, has a one-time $80 configuration fee, and requires no additional phone or software subscription. The business authorizes three additional paid preparation hours at $25 per hour. There is no tax, deposit or usage charge in this simplified example; a real budget must resolve those items.

| Fictional component | Before-launch cash | Later monthly run-rate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| First monthly subscription | $120 | $120 |
| One-time configuration | $80 | $0 |
| Additional paid preparation: 3 × $25 | $75 | $0 |
| **Known modeled total** | **$275** | **$120** |

Across three monthly payments, this model totals $120 × 3 + $80 + $75 = **$515**. Do not add the $275 launch figure to three further monthly payments unless you intentionally mean four paid months.

Suppose the owner also expects two hours to approve business instructions. Record those hours beside the budget. They are not another $50 cash payment unless the business actually incurs that additional payment. If you assign an opportunity-cost value for internal planning, show the assumption separately and avoid presenting it as money billed by the supplier.

sections.title: Decide which costs buy the launch you need
paragraphs:
For a residential service office, distinguish message-taking readiness from a supported booking workflow. Ask what must be configured, what your team must supply and which person accepts the result. A lower initial amount may buy a narrower scope; it does not prove better or worse value by itself.

Attach a deliverable to every configuration charge: the approved instruction set, supported calendar behavior, recipient arrangement or other agreed output. Include an owner and the evidence required before that work is accepted. The separate [onboarding readiness guide](/ai-answering-service/answering-service-onboarding) helps organize dependencies; this budget answers the financial commitment question.

Compare the plan you can maintain, not just the one you can activate. If paid assistance repeats, place it in recurring cost. If later changes are separately quoted, keep that uncertainty visible. This guide does not calculate savings or prove a payback period.

sections.title: Where Revo fits
paragraphs: [Revo's current pricing](/pricing) lists dedicated onboarding for Crew and Fleet, while Solo excludes it. That distinction does not establish a separate setup charge, a completion time or every supported connection. Confirm the actual assistance and required plan for your workflow. Do not convert a competitor's setup policy into a Revo promise.

sections.title: Frequently asked questions
paragraphs:
### Does no setup fee mean a zero-cost launch?

No. A required subscription payment, separately purchased service or incremental paid preparation can still require cash. Confirm the applicable offer and your own costs.

### Should annual prepayment be divided by twelve in the launch budget?

Use the amount actually due in the cash-needed view. A monthly equivalent can help compare recurring rates, but does not reduce the cash commitment due upfront.

### Can I budget a missing fee as zero?

No. Keep it unresolved, identify who must answer and decide whether it blocks your purchase. A provisional total is not an all-in quote.

[Compare current Revo plans](/pricing) with your completed launch-cost sheet and the reception scope your office needs.
